title: On the Complexity of Discounted Robust MDPs with $L_p$ Uncertainty Sets
claim: Measured iteration counts of policy iteration grow slowly with problem size and stay far below the worst-case theoretical bound.
layout: 2x2 grid of log-scale line plots, columns by uncertainty set, dashed bound on top
description: A 2x2 grid of line plots on log-scale y-axes. Columns are L1 uncertainty sets (left, panels a and c) and L-infinity uncertainty sets (right, panels b and d). The top row shows outer RMDP-PI iterations and the bottom row shows inner RMC-PI iterations. The x-axis is state-space size n, from about 0 to 256. Five colored lines with distinct markers mark the benchmarks: Gridworld (blue circles), Inventory (green squares), Machine Replacement (red triangles), GARNET (purple diamonds) and Long Chain (orange inverted triangles). A gray dashed curve for the theoretical upper bound sits far above all of them. The top row spans about 1 to 10^3 and the bottom row about 10 to 10^8. Most benchmarks stay nearly flat at a few iterations. Long Chain grows slowly but still sits well under the bound. A shared legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the dashed bound and the orange curve beneath it.
caption: Outer RMDP-PI (a, b) and total inner RMC-PI (c, d) iterations versus state-space size n on five benchmarks, under L1 (left) and L8 (right) uncertainty sets, with γ “ 0.5, δ “ 0.05. Dashed line: theoretical upper bound.
abstract: A basic model in sequential decision making is the Markov decision process (MDP), which is extended to Robust MDPs (RMDPs) by allowing uncertainty in transition probabilities and optimizing against the worst-case transition probabilities from the uncertainty sets. The class of $(s, a)$-rectangular RMDPs with $L_p$ uncertainty sets provides a flexible and expressive model for such problems. We study this class of RMDPs with a discounted-sum cost criterion and a constant discount factor. The existence of an efficient algorithm for this class is a fundamental theoretical question in optimization and sequential decision making. Previous results only establish a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for $L_\infty$ uncertainty sets. In this work, our main results are as follows: (a)~we show that for any compact uncertainty set, the policy iteration algorithm for RMDPs is strongly polynomial with oracle access to solutions of Robust Markov chains (RMCs); (b)~we present strongly polynomial-time bounds on the policy iteration algorithm for RMCs with $L_1$ and $L_\infty$ uncertainty sets; and (c)~we establish hardness results for RMCs with $L_p$ uncertainty sets for integer $p$ satisfying $1<p<\infty$. Finally, motivated by our theoretical bounds, we present experimental results showing how fast policy iteration converges for RMDPs with $L_1$ and $L_\infty$ uncertainty sets.
